newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto exchange group waters down disclosure plan.
newsitem.headline: Toronto exchange group waters down disclosure plan.

text.p: The Committee on Corporate Disclosure, sponsored by the Toronto Stock Exchange, said it tempered its suggestions for disclosure in a final report issued on Tuesday after consulting market players.

The committee, which heard from 125 firms, regulators and interested parties, said it recommended issuers, outside directors and officers face potential liabilty for misleading disclosure in oral discussions and "non-core" documents such as press releases.
Core documents include quarterly financial statements and material change reports.
The group, under the wing of Canada's largest equities market, also proposed a reduced "cap" on damages for officers and directors who are found liable.
The new "cap" is based on value at the time of the grant compared to the value of deferred compensation at the time of disclosure violation, it said.

The committee also outlined a lower basis of calculating potential liability of experts based on their revenue from the issuer, compared to the previous proposal of basing liability on C$1 million or three times their revenue, whichever is more.
The committee said it based its conclusions on the idea that "there is a sufficient degree of non-compliance with the current continuous disclosure rules in Canada to cause concern."

The final report discusses the creation of a limited statutory regime which would let injured investors bring civil actions against issuers and others who violate disclosure rules along with ways of improving Canada's regulatory network.
The committee presented an interim report in December, 1995.
